configuration.resource_amendment: Declared before examining LISA external recovery or prediction. The original twelve-hour ledger has 1254.29 seconds remaining. The completed GP-family control took 1634.24 seconds for evaluation alone; LISA additionally requires SNR event sampling and selection checks. Increase the cumulative ceiling by 1800 seconds to 12.5 hours and allow at most 2100 seconds for this evaluation, with one numerical thread and 2 GiB unchanged. Charge every preparation and failed attempt. This completes the original three-case comparison without changing priors, cases, outcomes, precision thresholds or posterior acceptance criteria.
configuration.decision: Use all 2000 weighted accepted copula draws and all accepted GP draws at both resolutions. Reuse verified 2048-sample test-event posteriors and the 256 copula predictions already evaluated on those samples. Verify the common 2048-sample training target against the independent archived 8192-sample events, retaining the original uniform, efficiency-extreme and largest-weight groups and independent fine selection fractions. Generate independent 8192-sample test events with the established four-batch sampler. Verify prediction on the same 64 ordered draws per copula chain, including training-target and selection refinement; verify GP prediction on every draw. Evaluate joint recovery on common 48/96 partitions, with independent transport and within-cell selection checks. Report all functional intervals, proper interval scores and both resolutions. No numerical choice or posterior is selected from scientific scores or injected truth.

precision_amendment.reason: The external target precision checks pass, but the NumPy/core equality check passed archived float32 event arrays to a helper that casts parameters to the event dtype. The accepted posterior was evaluated with float64 events. Repeat the core equality check with float64 events, matching the accepted inference and the NumPy evaluator. Preserve the failed float32 check and its full process cost. Reuse only the unchanged NumPy training integrals and their derived differences byte for byte. Keep the 1e-6 equality threshold and every scientific comparison requirement unchanged. No LISA scientific score has yet been evaluated. The 1780-second continuation plus the 311.95-second first attempt stays within the original 2100-second evaluation allocation.
